easy.explanation: The Lord says, “Behold, I will send my messenger, and he shall prepare the way before me.”
easy.q: Who is sent to prepare the way before the Lord?

easy.explanation: The passage says that he “shall purify the sons of Levi.”

answers: Sorcerers, adulterers, false swearers, and oppressors
easy.explanation: The Lord lists sorcerers, adulterers, false swearers, and those who oppress vulnerable people.
easy.q: Against whom will the Lord be a swift witness?

answers: To prepare the way before the Lord
medium.explanation: The messenger is sent to prepare the way before the Lord’s coming.
medium.q: What is the messenger’s role according to the passage?

answers: So they may offer an offering in righteousness
So they may escape all judgment
medium.explanation: They are purified “that they may offer unto the Lord an offering in righteousness.”
medium.q: Why are the sons of Levi purified?

medium.explanation: The refiner’s fire illustrates the cleansing and testing of the sons of Levi.
medium.q: What does the refiner’s fire represent in this passage?

answers: The messenger prepares the way, the Levites are purified, and the Lord comes to judgment
Judgment comes, then the messenger is sent, and the temple is rebuilt
The Levites offer first, then the Lord leaves, and the messenger comes
challenge.explanation: The passage moves from the messenger’s preparation to purification and then to the Lord’s judgment.
challenge.q: What sequence is presented in the passage?

answers: Purification enables them to offer acceptably in righteousness
challenge.explanation: The Levites are purified so that their offering may be righteous and pleasing to the Lord.
challenge.q: How does the purification of the sons of Levi relate to their offering?

answers: It includes oppression of the vulnerable
challenge.explanation: The Lord judges those who oppress the hireling, widow, fatherless, and stranger.
challenge.q: What feature of the Lord’s judgment is emphasized in verse 5?

paragraphs.title: God’s Faithfulness and the Call to Repentance

easy.explanation: The Lord declares, “For I am the Lord, I change not.”
easy.q: What does the Lord say about Himself?

answers: They had gone away from them
They had replaced them with new ones
easy.explanation: The passage says, “ye are gone away from mine ordinances, and have not kept them.”
easy.q: What had the people done to the Lord’s ordinances?

easy.explanation: The Lord commands, “Return unto me, and I will return unto you.”
easy.q: What does the Lord tell the people to do?

answers: They are not consumed because the Lord does not change
They become kings because the Lord changes
They do not need repentance because the Lord changes
medium.explanation: The verse connects “I change not” with the fact that the sons of Jacob are not consumed.
medium.q: How are the Lord’s unchanging nature and the sons of Jacob connected?

answers: You have departed from God’s laws
medium.explanation: To go away from the ordinances means to depart from or disobey them.
medium.q: What does “ye are gone away from mine ordinances” mean?

answers: They do not recognize their wrongdoing
They refuse to speak at all
medium.explanation: Their question suggests that they do not understand or acknowledge how they have gone astray.
medium.q: What does the people’s question, “Wherein shall we return?” suggest?

answers: The Lord is faithful, but the people have departed from His ordinances
The people are faithful, but the Lord changes
Both the Lord and the people abandon the ordinances
challenge.explanation: The Lord says He does not change, while the people are described as having gone away from His ordinances.
challenge.q: What central contrast appears in the passage?

answers: Repentance brings renewed fellowship with God
challenge.explanation: The wording presents a mutual return: the people are called to return to God, and He promises to return to them.
challenge.q: What does “Return unto me, and I will return unto you” imply?

answers: They fail to recognize their sin
They want to punish the righteous
challenge.explanation: Their question, “Wherein shall we return?” reveals a lack of awareness concerning their disobedience.
challenge.q: What spiritual problem is revealed by the people’s response?

easy.explanation: The Lord says, “In tithes and offerings.”
easy.q: In what had the people robbed God?

easy.explanation: The command is, “Bring ye all the tithes into the storehouse.”
easy.q: Where were the people commanded to bring all the tithes?

easy.explanation: The Lord promises to open “the windows of heaven” and pour out a blessing.
easy.q: What did the Lord promise to open?

medium.explanation: The purpose was “that there may be meat in mine house.”
medium.q: What was to be found in God’s house when the tithes were brought?

answers: Robbing God in tithes and offerings
medium.explanation: The nation is cursed because it has robbed God by withholding the tithes and offerings.
medium.q: What does the curse in this passage result from?

answers: The devourer would not destroy the fruits of the ground
The people would never face war
The people would leave the land
medium.explanation: The Lord promises to rebuke the devourer so that the fruits of the ground will not be destroyed.
medium.q: What protection would follow the Lord’s blessing?

answers: They provide meat in God’s house and accompany protection for the land’s fruit
They replace worship and destroy the harvest
They are intended only for wealthy people
challenge.explanation: The tithes provide meat in God’s house, while the Lord promises protection for the ground and vine.
challenge.q: How do the tithes relate both to worship and to agriculture?

answers: Bringing all the tithes into the storehouse
challenge.explanation: The command to bring all the tithes comes before the promise to open the windows of heaven.
challenge.q: What condition is stated before the promise of blessing?

challenge.explanation: The phrase describes a blessing so abundant that there will not be enough room to contain it.
challenge.q: What does the promise of blessing “that there shall not be room enough to receive it” communicate?

paragraphs.title: The People’s Complaints and the Book of Remembrance

easy.explanation: They said, “It is vain to serve God.”
easy.q: What did the people say about serving God?

easy.explanation: The passage says, “Then they that feared the Lord spake often one to another.”
easy.q: Who spoke often to one another?

easy.explanation: A book of remembrance was written for those who feared the Lord and thought upon His name.
easy.q: What was written before the Lord?

answers: They saw the proud and wicked prosper
medium.explanation: They called the proud happy and observed that those who worked wickedness were set up and delivered.
medium.q: Why did the people complain that serving God brought no profit?

answers: They encouraged one another by speaking together
medium.explanation: They spoke often to one another, and the Lord listened and heard them.
medium.q: What did those who feared the Lord do in response?

medium.explanation: The Lord says they will be His in the day when He makes up His jewels, meaning His treasured possession.
medium.q: What does “my jewels” mean in this context?

answers: The complainers doubt the value of serving God, while the faithful encourage one another
challenge.explanation: The complainers focus on the apparent success of the wicked, while those who fear the Lord continue speaking faithfully to one another.
challenge.q: What contrast appears between the complainers and those who fear the Lord?

answers: To record the words and faithfulness of those who fear the Lord
To record only the sins of the wicked
challenge.explanation: The book records those who feared the Lord and thought upon His name, in connection with the coming day of distinction.
challenge.q: What is the purpose of the book of remembrance?

answers: The Lord will spare them as a man spares his son
They will be punished with the wicked
They will disappear from the land
challenge.explanation: The Lord promises, “I will spare them, as a man spareth his own son that serveth him.”
challenge.q: What promise is given to those who fear the Lord?

paragraphs.title: The Day of God and the Sun of Righteousness

easy.explanation: The day is described as “burning as an oven,” or furnace.
easy.q: What is the coming day compared to?

answers: They will be crowned as kings
easy.explanation: The wicked will become ashes under the feet of the righteous.
easy.q: What will happen to the wicked on that day?

easy.explanation: The passage promises that “the Sun of righteousness” will arise for them.
easy.q: What will arise for those who fear the Lord’s name?

answers: The wicked are burned, while the righteous receive healing and joy
The wicked receive healing while the righteous are destroyed
medium.explanation: The wicked are consumed like stubble, while the Sun of righteousness brings healing to those who fear God.
medium.q: What is the difference between the fate of the wicked and the righteous?

answers: A fire that consumes the righteous
medium.explanation: The Sun of righteousness has “healing in his wings,” presenting restoration and blessing.
medium.q: What does the “Sun of righteousness” represent in context?

answers: They will go forth and grow up as calves of the stall
medium.explanation: The passage says they “shall go forth, and grow up as calves of the stall.”
medium.q: What will those who fear the Lord do after the Sun of righteousness arises?

answers: The complete and swift destruction of the wicked
challenge.explanation: The day will burn the wicked like stubble, leaving neither root nor branch.
challenge.q: What does the image of fire and stubble emphasize?

answers: No lasting remnant or continuation will remain
The wicked will grow like trees
challenge.explanation: The image of root and branch indicates that the wicked will have no enduring continuation.
challenge.q: What does “leave them neither root nor branch” mean?

answers: It contrasts the humiliation of the wicked with the joyful freedom of the righteous
It gives everyone the same fate
It removes the distinction between good and evil
challenge.explanation: The wicked become ashes, while those who fear God go forth joyfully under the healing Sun of righteousness.
challenge.q: How does the image of ashes relate to the promise for those who fear God?

paragraphs.title: The Torah of Moses and Elijah, Herald of Redemption

easy.explanation: The passage says, “Remember ye the law of Moses my servant.”
easy.q: Whose law were the people commanded to remember?

easy.explanation: The Lord promises, “I will send you Elijah the prophet.”
easy.q: Whom would the Lord send before the great and dreadful day?

easy.explanation: Elijah will turn “the heart of the fathers to the children, and the heart of the children to their fathers.”
easy.q: Between whom would Elijah turn the hearts?

medium.explanation: The law is described as containing “the statutes and judgments” given to Israel.
medium.q: What does Moses’ law include according to the passage?

medium.explanation: Turning hearts toward one another suggests renewed love, unity, and reconciliation.
medium.q: What does turning the hearts of fathers and children suggest?

answers: Before the coming of the great and dreadful day of the Lord
Before the tithes enter the storehouse
medium.explanation: Elijah is promised before the great and dreadful day of the Lord.
medium.q: Before which event would Elijah be sent?

answers: Remembering Moses’ law and restoring relationships prepare the people for the Lord’s day
Leaving the law and separating families prepare the people
Bringing tithes and rebuilding the storehouse prepare the people
challenge.explanation: The conclusion joins faithfulness to Moses’ law with restored hearts and preparation for the day of the Lord.
challenge.q: How are the two commands at the end of the book connected?

answers: To prepare the people through renewed hearts and repentance
To judge the wicked by himself
challenge.explanation: Elijah’s ministry turns hearts toward one another before the Lord’s day, pointing to preparation and repentance.
challenge.q: What is Elijah’s role according to the passage?

answers: The Lord will smite the earth with a curse
The land will become a delightful land
The windows of heaven will open
challenge.explanation: The passage ends with the warning, “lest I come and smite the earth with a curse.”
challenge.q: What warning is given if the hearts are not turned?
